properties.Lithology, structures, paleowind: i) Lower Bima - fault controlled conglomerates, sands and gravels with poorly defined internal structures, and characterized by well-defined fining-upward successions. Trough cross beds are common in association with minor tabular units. Red, grey and dark clay/shales with fine to medium grained sandstones were reported as lacustrine deposit; ii) Middle Bima ?medium to very coarse grained feldspathic sandstones with trough and tabular cross bedding interbedded with clays; iii) Upper Bima - planar cross bedded, medium to coarse grained sandstone that shows soft sediment deformation structures.
properties.Paleoenvironment: Continental: i) Lower Bima ?lacustrine, marginal lacustrine, alluvial-braided; ii) Middle Bima ?fluvial braided; iii) Upper Bima - fluvial braided
properties.Fossil occurrences: N/A
properties.Geochemistry data: Organic geochemical: The n-alkane patterns of the analysed shale samples show a bimodal distribution with a predominance of long-chain n-alkanes molecular weight compounds (n-C22-n-C28), indicating mixed organic matter with a significant contribution of terrestrial organic matter. The Tm/Ts ratios of 1.3e1.8 in the samples further indicate that the samples contain a mixture of aquatic organic matter and land plants. In most of the analysed samples, the C27 and C29 steranes predominate over the C28 steranes, reflecting a mixed contribution of aquatic algae and microorganisms with a significant amount of land plant as indicated by the regular sterane ratio ternary diagram. The Pr/Ph ratios (1.04-1.90) of the organic matter in the Bima shale sediments suggest deposition under sub-oxic to relatively anoxic conditions. The shale samples have low Sr/Ba ratio (avg. 0.24), indicating low salinity water during sedimentation. Inorganic geochemical: The Sr/Cu ratios of the studied shales (average 6.4) indicate a hot-arid climate.
properties.Climate assignment leading evidence: Alluvial - fluvial braided and Sr/Cu ratios
